risk: Recorded inventory does not reflect what is physically held or what it is genuinely worth, misstating both the balance sheet and margin.
audit_objective: Verify that inventory exists, is owned, is counted accurately, and is valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
what_to_review: Count programme coverage, independence and adjustment approval
Goods in transit and consignment stock ownership
Cost build-up and overhead absorption
Net realisable value testing on slow-moving and damaged stock
Third-party locations and stock held by others
procedures: Attend counts at a sample of locations; re-perform test counts in both directions, floor to sheet and sheet to floor.
Test cut-off around the period end for goods received and despatched.
Obtain confirmations for stock held at third parties and reconcile to the ledger.
Recompute the cost build-up for a sample of items including overhead absorption, and compare cost to recent selling prices net of costs to sell.
Analyse adjustment postings for entries made outside the count process.
red_flags: Adjustments posted just after a count to restore the book figure
Consignment stock recorded as owned
Overhead absorption rates unchanged despite volume shifts
Locations never selected for count
plain: Stock is often the largest number on the balance sheet, and it is only worth what it can actually be sold for.

risk: Capital spend is approved on optimistic business cases, overruns without escalation, and assets on the register can no longer be located.
audit_objective: Assess whether capital investment is authorised, controlled against budget, and whether recorded assets physically exist.
what_to_review: Business case quality and post-implementation review
Approval authority and project change control
Capitalisation timing and classification
Physical verification programme
Disposals, transfers and idle assets
procedures: Select major projects and compare approved business case benefits to post-implementation actuals; test whether reviews are performed at all.
Test overruns against the re-approval threshold and inspect evidence of escalation.
Physically verify a sample of recorded assets and, in reverse, trace observed assets back to the register.
Test the capitalisation date against evidence the asset was available for use.
Review idle and fully depreciated assets still in service for impairment or life reassessment.
red_flags: Post-implementation reviews never performed
Projects split to stay under an approval threshold
Assets on the register nobody can locate
Capitalisation dated before commissioning
evidence: Capital approval papers and business cases
plain: Big capital projects get approved on promises, and almost nobody goes back to check whether the promises came true.

risk: Bank mandates, payment authority and hedging activity are not controlled, exposing the organisation to fraud and to unmanaged market risk.
audit_objective: Confirm that banking arrangements, payment authority and treasury activity operate within board-approved mandates.
what_to_review: Bank account inventory and signatory mandates
Payment release authority and dual authorisation
Treasury policy limits on counterparty, currency and interest exposure
Hedging authorisation and effectiveness
Cash forecasting accuracy and idle balances
procedures: Obtain a complete list of bank accounts from the banks themselves, not from the ledger, and reconcile to the recorded accounts.
Test current signatory mandates against the approved authority list and identify leavers still holding authority.
Test that payment release genuinely requires two independent approvers, including for urgent and manual payments.
Compare open treasury positions to policy limits at several dates and test breach escalation.
Compare cash forecasts to actuals and assess forecasting discipline.
red_flags: Bank accounts not in the ledger
Leavers still on mandates
Urgent payments routinely bypassing dual authorisation
Positions repeatedly at or just inside limits
plain: Bank accounts and payment authority are the front door to the company's cash.

risk: Returns are filed late or on incorrect positions, and intercompany pricing is not supported by documentation, leading to assessments, interest and penalties.
audit_objective: Assess whether tax obligations are identified and met on time and whether positions taken are documented and defensible.
what_to_review: Tax obligation calendar completeness across all jurisdictions
Filing and payment timeliness
Uncertain tax positions and provisioning
Transfer pricing policy, documentation and actual pricing applied
Indirect tax coding accuracy on transactions
procedures: Build the obligation calendar independently from entity and jurisdiction data and compare to the one in use.
Test filing and payment dates against statutory deadlines and quantify interest and penalties incurred.
Review uncertain tax positions and test whether the provision reflects current authority correspondence.
Test whether intercompany transactions were actually priced per the transfer pricing policy and whether local file documentation exists.
Sample transactions and re-perform indirect tax coding.
red_flags: Obligations discovered only when the authority writes
Penalties recurring in the same jurisdiction
Transfer pricing documentation prepared long after year end
Manual overrides of tax codes at invoice entry
plain: Filing tax late or on the wrong basis costs interest and penalties, and repeats every year until it is fixed.

risk: Manual journal entries are used to force results to expectation, and the close is completed too quickly for controls to operate meaningfully.
audit_objective: Evaluate the integrity of the financial close, focusing on manual adjustments and account reconciliation quality.
what_to_review: Manual journal authorisation, support and posting rights
Top-side and consolidation adjustments
Balance sheet reconciliation completion and review quality
Close timetable versus control operation
Estimates and accruals with judgement
procedures: Extract all manual journals and analyse by preparer, value, account, and posting date and time; test round-sum entries, entries posted at unusual hours, and entries to income statement accounts near period end.
Test that each sampled journal has support and an approver independent of the preparer.
Sample balance sheet reconciliations and reassess whether reconciling items are genuinely explained or simply labelled.
Compare journal patterns across periods to identify entries appearing only when results are close to target.
red_flags: Journals posted after the close was reported as complete
Recurring entries with the description "reclass" and no support
Reconciliations signed the same day they were prepared
Late adjustments always moving in the favourable direction
evidence: Full journal entry extract with user and timestamp
plain: Manual journals are how results get adjusted at the last minute, which makes them the first place to look.

risk: Critical activities are outsourced without contractual protection, assurance over the provider, or a viable exit, so failures land back on the organisation.
audit_objective: Assess whether third parties performing critical activities are selected, contracted and monitored proportionately to the risk they carry.
what_to_review: Inventory of third parties and criticality assessment
Due diligence performed before contracting
Contract terms — service levels, audit rights, data protection, exit
Ongoing assurance such as service auditor reports and site visits
Concentration risk and exit planning
procedures: Build an independent inventory of third parties from accounts payable and compare it to the register maintained by the business.
For critical providers, test that pre-contract due diligence was performed and documented.
Review contracts for audit rights, service levels, data protection and termination assistance.
Obtain service auditor reports for critical providers and test that complementary user controls were actually implemented.
Test whether exit plans exist and are credible for the most concentrated dependencies.
red_flags: Critical providers absent from the register
Contracts auto-renewing without review
Service auditor reports received but never read
Exceptions in those reports with no follow-up
No alternative provider identified for a single point of dependency
kpis: % critical providers with current due diligence
plain: Outsourcing the work never outsources the responsibility. When the supplier fails, it is still your problem.

risk: People are hired without verification of their credentials, retain access and entitlements after leaving, and exit obligations are not enforced.
audit_objective: Assess whether the employee lifecycle is controlled from pre-hire screening through to exit.
what_to_review: Pre-employment screening — identity, right to work, qualifications, references, criminal record where permitted
Approval of new positions against approved headcount
Onboarding: contract, code of conduct, mandatory training
Exit: access removal, asset return, final pay, restrictive covenants
Contractor and contingent worker treatment
procedures: Sample new hires and test that every required screening step was completed before the start date, not after.
Verify professional qualifications directly with the issuing body for roles where they are a condition of employment.
Reconcile headcount to approved positions and investigate roles filled without approval.
Sample leavers and test the elapsed time to access removal, asset return and final settlement.
Test whether contractors are subject to equivalent screening for equivalent access.
red_flags: Screening completed weeks after the start date
Qualifications accepted on a photocopy
Leavers retaining building or system access
Contractors engaged for years through rolling short contracts
Exit interviews not conducted for regretted leavers
plain: Hiring someone without checking who they are, and letting leavers keep access, are both simple failures with expensive consequences.

risk: Pay decisions, incentives and promotions are made inconsistently, and behavioural issues are not addressed, driving turnover, grievance and conduct risk.
audit_objective: Evaluate whether reward and performance processes are applied consistently and whether conduct concerns are dealt with.
what_to_review: Salary review and promotion decision governance
Incentive plan design and payout calculation
Pay equity across comparable roles
Performance management completion and quality
Grievance, disciplinary and harassment case handling
procedures: Recompute a sample of incentive payouts against plan rules and approved performance outcomes.
Analyse pay across comparable roles for unexplained dispersion, and test the explanations offered.
Test performance review completion rates and read a sample for substance rather than box-ticking.
Review grievance and disciplinary cases for investigation independence, timeliness and consistency of outcome.
Compare voluntary turnover by manager and function against the organisational average.
red_flags: Incentives paid despite unmet performance conditions
Turnover concentrated under specific managers
Grievances against senior staff investigated by their own reports
Performance ratings clustered with no differentiation
plain: How people are paid and promoted drives how they behave, which shapes every other control in the business.
